brief.meaningEn: Make a conspicuous display mainly to impress observers rather than because of sincere care.
brief.meaningZh: 主要為了取悅旁觀者而刻意做場面，並非出於真誠關懷。
brief.grammar: Put on a show / putting on a show; distinguish the performative display sense from literally staging entertainment or starting playback.
brief.register: Candid family-event discussion: a sister tells her brother to keep their parents’ anniversary gathering thoughtful instead of staging a display for social media.
brief.boundaryZh: 有漂亮佈置不一定是假；要看是否把給人看凌駕於真誠目的。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是指真的表演節目，也不同於只播放影片的 put on。
brief.outcomeZh: 能以行動目的判斷真誠照顧與為觀眾做場面。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 78, row 5; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The gathering is about care, not putting on a show.

listening.en: The hosts hired photographers to film every gift but barely spoke to the guest of honour. It felt like putting on a show rather than caring for her.
listening.zh: 主人請攝影師拍下每份禮物，卻幾乎沒跟主角說話。這更像做場面給人看，而非關心她。
listening.promptZh: putting on a show 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: Creating a display to impress onlookers more than to care for her.
options.zh: 做場面令旁人留下印象，多於關心她。

options.en: Staging a theatre performance for the guest.
options.zh: 為主角演一齣舞台劇。

options.en: Starting a film on a screen.
options.zh: 在螢幕播放電影。

options.en: Quietly asking what she actually wants.
options.zh: 私下詢問她真正想要甚麼。

listening.explanationZh: 重點是拍攝給人看，卻忽略主角。

reply.promptEn: Why did Nia choose a small meal rather than a filmed ceremony? Her grandmother wanted time to talk with family; the large event would focus on dramatic entrances for viewers.
reply.promptZh: （妮雅為何選小型聚餐而非拍攝典禮？祖母希望與家人交談；大型活動則會著重給觀眾看的戲劇化進場。）

options.en: The meal better matches her grandmother’s wish for conversation.
options.zh: 聚餐較符合祖母想交談的願望。

options.en: The filmed entrance would prioritise appearances.
options.zh: 拍攝進場會把場面放在首位。

options.en: Nia does not want to put on a show for viewers.
options.zh: 妮雅不想為觀眾做場面。

options.en: The family can give attention to the person being honoured.
options.zh: 家人可以關注受慶祝的主角。

reply.explanationZh: 四句都以主角需要對照觀眾場面；金句用 put on a show。

scene.promptZh: 義工為了照片排長龍，卻沒有把食物交給等候的人。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The photo queue risks putting on a show instead of meeting people’s needs.
options.zh: 排隊拍照恐怕是在做場面，而非滿足人們需要。

options.en: The volunteers are literally staging a play.
options.zh: 義工真的在演戲。

options.en: The people have already received all their meals.
options.zh: 大家已收到全部餐點。

scene.explanationZh: 只顧照片而沒有提供服務，支持做場面之判斷。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以說是 put on a show？

options.en: A team spends all its effort on camera angles and ignores clients.
options.zh: 團隊只顧鏡頭角度，忽略服務對象。

options.en: A host decorates the room and still spends the evening listening to guests.
options.zh: 主人佈置房間後，整晚仍用心聽客人說話。

options.en: An organiser stages a public display while omitting the promised help.
options.zh: 籌辦人安排公開場面，卻不提供承諾的協助。

contrast.explanationZh: 漂亮佈置可與真誠關心並存。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「只要有漂亮佈置，就是做場面。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: A lovely room is not necessarily putting on a show; the purpose and care shown to guests matter.
options.zh: 漂亮場地不一定是做場面；要看目的和對客人的關心。

options.en: Every decoration proves the host is insincere.
options.zh: 任何佈置都證明主人不真誠。

options.en: The phrase only means playing a video.
options.zh: 這片語只表示播放影片。

dialogue.explanationZh: 應看展示是否取代真誠照顧。

speaking.en: They stopped putting on a show for the cameras and spent the afternoon helping the families who had come.
speaking.zh: 他們不再為鏡頭做場面，轉而花整個下午協助到場家庭。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出改變前後的目的。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：校園慈善日的主辦人原想請人拍攝巨型支票交接，但受助學生更需要安靜的功課輔導；團隊改為提供輔導，只簡單公布捐款。用一至兩句英文說明選擇，不要說所有拍照都不真誠。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出放棄巨型支票場面、提供功課輔導、簡單公布捐款；勿一概否定拍照。

examples.en: Instead of putting on a show with a giant cheque, the team offered quiet homework support and announced the donation simply.
examples.zh: 團隊沒有拿巨型支票做場面，而是提供安靜的功課輔導，並簡單公布捐款。

examples.en: The organisers dropped the filmed giant-cheque handover rather than put on a show for the cameras: they gave pupils homework help and kept the donation announcement brief.
examples.zh: 主辦人放棄拍攝巨型支票交接，不為鏡頭做場面：他們為學生提供功課輔導，並簡短公布捐款。

takeaways.en: Putting on a show focuses on impressing observers rather than the person served.
takeaways.zh: 做場面是重視旁觀者印象多於服務對象。

takeaways.en: A lovely room is not automatically putting on a show.
takeaways.zh: 呈現得漂亮本身不證明不真誠。

brief.meaningEn: More than a person or group can afford from its available resources.
brief.meaningZh: 超出個人或團體的財力負擔。
brief.grammar: Spend/live beyond one’s means; means is plural and refers to financial resources, not a method.
brief.register: Practical budgeting advice: a community finance volunteer discusses wedding costs with a couple who want to avoid borrowing for extras.
brief.boundaryZh: 花費高不一定超出負擔能力；要與實際預算和資源比較。
brief.misconceptionZh: means 在此不是「方法」；亦不能單憑價格猜測別人的財務狀況。
brief.outcomeZh: 能比較支出與可用預算，而非只比較場面大小。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 79, row 2; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: Couples should not spend beyond their means.

listening.en: The couple could pay for a simple meal, but the luxury venue would require a loan they could not repay. They decided not to spend beyond their means.
listening.zh: 這對新人付得起簡單聚餐，但租用豪華場地便要借無法償還的款項。他們決定不花超出負擔能力的錢。
listening.promptZh: beyond their means 表示甚麼？

options.en: More than the couple can afford.
options.zh: 超出這對新人的財力負擔。

options.en: More than they know how to organise.
options.zh: 超出他們懂得籌辦的方法。

options.en: Any celebration that looks elegant.
options.zh: 任何看起來高雅的慶祝。

options.en: A cost that they already saved enough to cover.
options.zh: 他們已存夠錢支付的費用。

listening.explanationZh: 要借無法償還的款項，表示支出超出負擔。

reply.promptEn: Why did the club cancel the expensive coach trip? Its budget covers a local visit, but the trip would need debt that next year’s membership fees could not repay.
reply.promptZh: （學會為何取消昂貴的旅遊車行程？預算足以支付本地參觀，但旅遊車行程需借款，來年的會費也無法還清。）

options.en: The coach trip exceeds what the club can afford.
options.zh: 旅遊車行程超出學會能負擔的費用。

options.en: The local visit fits the current budget.
options.zh: 本地參觀符合目前預算。

options.en: The club should not spend beyond its means.
options.zh: 學會不應花超出負擔能力的錢。

options.en: Avoiding unrepayable debt explains the decision.
options.zh: 避免無法償還的債務，解釋了這項決定。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均以預算和還款能力作根據；金句用 beyond its means。

scene.promptZh: 家庭每月可用二千元作旅行開支，卻打算每月支付五千元旅費並持續借款。哪句最貼切？

options.en: They would be spending beyond their means.
options.zh: 他們會花超出負擔能力的錢。

options.en: They have already saved enough for the trip.
options.zh: 他們已存夠旅費。

options.en: The trip must be poorly organised.
options.zh: 旅行一定安排得很差。

scene.explanationZh: 費用大於可用預算，且需持續借款。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個情況最不足以證明 beyond their means？

options.en: A family borrows repeatedly to pay for optional extras it cannot repay.
options.zh: 家庭反覆借款支付無法償還的額外開支。

options.en: A family uses savings set aside for a trip and keeps its essential bills covered.
options.zh: 家庭用預留旅費的儲蓄旅行，仍能支付必要帳單。

options.en: A club books equipment costing twice its available budget without new funding.
options.zh: 學會無新資金，卻預訂價格為預算兩倍的器材。

contrast.explanationZh: 有儲蓄且必要開支受保障，不足以說超出負擔。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「婚宴很漂亮，所以一定超出他們能力。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: Looking elegant does not prove they spent beyond their means; compare the cost with what they can afford.
options.zh: 單看外觀不足判斷；要比較費用和他們可負擔的金額。

options.en: Beautiful events always require debt.
options.zh: 漂亮活動必然要借款。

options.en: Means here refers to event-planning methods.
options.zh: 這裏的 means 指籌辦方法。

dialogue.explanationZh: 判斷要以資源與支出為準。

speaking.en: They chose a modest celebration rather than spending beyond their means on a venue that required a loan.
speaking.zh: 他們選擇簡樸慶祝，沒有為要借款的場地花超出負擔能力的錢。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出哪項費用會造成壓力。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：學生劇團有一萬元資助，可支付校內舞台和服裝；租外面劇院要三萬元，而且沒有額外捐款。團隊選校內演出。用一至兩句英文解釋財務理由，不要批評外面劇院本身。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出一萬元預算、外面劇院需三萬元且無新捐款、選校內舞台避免超支。

examples.en: With a ten-thousand-dollar grant and no additional donations, the troupe would spend beyond its means on a thirty-thousand-dollar theatre, so it chose the school stage.
examples.zh: 劇團只有一萬元資助，也沒有額外捐款；花三萬元租劇院便會超出負擔能力，因此選擇校內舞台。

examples.en: The outside theatre costs thirty thousand dollars, while the grant is only ten thousand with no new donations; the troupe avoided spending beyond its means by performing at school.
examples.zh: 外面劇院要三萬元，資助卻只有一萬元，而且沒有新捐款；劇團選擇在學校演出，避免花超出負擔能力的錢。

takeaways.en: Spending beyond their means exceeds their available resources.
takeaways.zh: 超出負擔能力，要比較支出與可用資源。

takeaways.en: An expensive choice is not necessarily beyond their means when they can afford it.
takeaways.zh: 昂貴選擇並非對所有人都超出負擔能力。

brief.meaningEn: A moment felt to be exceptionally rare and not expected to recur in the same way.
brief.meaningZh: 令人感到極其難得、料想不會以同樣方式重現的一刻。
brief.grammar: Once-in-a-lifetime is a compound adjective before moment/opportunity; a wedding can feel this way without a literal guarantee that no similar event will occur.
brief.register: Warm personal speech: a sibling explains why the family wants to mark a unique graduation reunion thoughtfully, without claiming every costly extra is necessary.
brief.boundaryZh: 強調珍貴與罕見，不等於昂貴才值得，也不保證人生絕不再有相似時刻。
brief.misconceptionZh: 不是「一生只准一次」的法律規則；也不能用它直接證明任何開支合理。
brief.outcomeZh: 能表達難得時刻，同時避免由珍貴推論必須豪花。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 79, row 3; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: A wedding can feel like one of life's once-in-a-lifetime moments.

listening.en: After years apart, the whole family gathered to celebrate her graduation. For her, seeing everyone together was one of those once-in-a-lifetime moments.
listening.zh: 分隔多年後，全家聚首慶祝她畢業。對她而言，見到所有人團聚，是一生難得的一刻。
listening.promptZh: once-in-a-lifetime moments 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: Exceptionally rare and personally memorable occasions.
options.zh: 非常難得、值得個人銘記的時刻。

options.en: Occasions that require a luxury venue.
options.zh: 必須租豪華場地的時刻。

options.en: Moments that are legally permitted only once.
options.zh: 法律上只准發生一次的時刻。

options.en: Ordinary weekly family meals.
options.zh: 每星期普通的家庭聚餐。

listening.explanationZh: 多年後全家聚首，重點是難得而珍貴。

reply.promptEn: Why did Priya keep a small photograph from the reunion? Three generations met for the first time, and the eldest relative could travel only on that occasion.
reply.promptZh: （普麗雅為何保留聚會的小照片？三代人首次見面，最年長的親人亦只有那次能出行。）

options.en: The gathering was unusually rare for the family.
options.zh: 這次聚會對家庭而言非常難得。

options.en: The photograph helps her remember a special meeting.
options.zh: 照片讓她記住這次特別相聚。

options.en: It felt like a once-in-a-lifetime moment to Priya.
options.zh: 對普麗雅而言，那像是一生難得的一刻。

options.en: The chance for all three generations to meet was exceptional.
options.zh: 三代同堂的機會十分難得。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均以三代首次同聚和難以重來為根據；金句用 once-in-a-lifetime moment。

scene.promptZh: 運動員首次代表家鄉出賽，全鎮親友在終點迎接她；她覺得極其難忘。哪句最合適？

options.en: She may describe the welcome as a once-in-a-lifetime moment.
options.zh: 她可能形容這次迎接為一生難得的一刻。

options.en: The welcome proves she will never race again.
options.zh: 這次迎接證明她永遠不會再比賽。

options.en: The phrase means the welcome must have cost a lot.
options.zh: 這說法表示迎接活動必定花費高昂。

scene.explanationZh: 可表達個人珍貴感受，不必預言未來。

contrast.promptZh: 哪個例子最不適合這個說法？

options.en: A family reunites across three countries after twenty years.
options.zh: 家人相隔二十年後跨三國重聚。

options.en: A commuter catches the same bus at the same stop every weekday.
options.zh: 通勤者每個工作天都在同一站乘同一班巴士。

options.en: A student hears her name called at a rare award ceremony.
options.zh: 學生在難得的頒獎禮聽到自己的名字。

contrast.explanationZh: 每天重複的例行事，沒有特別罕見的依據。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「既然是 once-in-a-lifetime，就一定要借錢辦最貴的慶祝。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: A once-in-a-lifetime moment can be meaningful without unaffordable spending.
options.zh: 一生難得的一刻可以意義深刻，毋須花超出負擔能力的錢。

options.en: Rare moments always justify any amount of debt.
options.zh: 難得時刻一定值得承擔任何債務。

options.en: An inexpensive gathering cannot be memorable.
options.zh: 不昂貴的聚會不可能令人難忘。

dialogue.explanationZh: 難得與昂貴之間沒有必然關係。

speaking.en: Hearing her father sing with her children felt like a once-in-a-lifetime moment, even in their small kitchen.
speaking.zh: 在小廚房裏聽父親和孩子一起唱歌，對她而言像是一生難得的一刻。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出珍貴感是否取決於場地價格。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：多年分居的三姊妹終於在母親七十歲生日同桌吃飯；家中簡單煮食，沒有豪華場地，但她們十分珍惜這次相聚。用一至兩句英文描述時刻的意義，勿聲稱絕對不會再聚。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出三姊妹多年後與母親相聚、簡單家宴仍珍貴，避免絕對預言。

examples.en: After years apart, the sisters’ simple dinner with their mother on her seventieth birthday felt like a once-in-a-lifetime moment, even without a grand venue.
examples.zh: 多年分居後，三姊妹在母親七十歲生日與她吃的簡單晚餐像是一生難得的一刻，即使沒有豪華場地。

examples.en: After years apart, the three sisters treasured their mother’s seventieth birthday meal at home as a once-in-a-lifetime moment; its value came from meeting again, not the cost.
examples.zh: 多年分居後，三姊妹珍惜在家為母親慶祝七十歲生日的飯局，視之為一生難得的一刻；珍貴之處在於重聚，不在花費。

takeaways.en: A once-in-a-lifetime moment feels exceptionally rare to the person involved.
takeaways.zh: 一生難得強調對當事人而言非常罕見。

takeaways.en: A once-in-a-lifetime moment need not require an expensive celebration.
takeaways.zh: 難得時刻不必以昂貴慶祝來證明。

brief.meaningEn: Money used for a result that the speaker judges worthwhile.
brief.meaningZh: 某筆錢帶來說話者認為值得的成果。
brief.grammar: Call/consider something money well spent; spent is a past participle modifying money. State the benefit, not merely the price.
brief.register: Public-budget discussion: a resident explains to a council member why accessible seating at a local festival justified its cost.
brief.boundaryZh: 這是有理由的價值判斷，不是「便宜」的同義詞，也不保證每個人同意。
brief.misconceptionZh: 錢花光了不等於花得值得；須指出所得成果。
brief.outcomeZh: 能把開支連到具體好處，並區分花得值與只因價格低。

sources.file: Idiomatic and Natural English Expressions Books 10 to 16 Part 3.docx
sources.locatorNote: DOCX table 80, row 7; page refers to the locally rendered PDF recorded in the intake summary.
sources.sentence: The community festival was money well spent.

listening.en: The community festival paid for ramps so wheelchair users could reach every activity. Many residents called the accessibility work money well spent.
listening.zh: 社區節慶付費設置斜道，讓輪椅使用者能到達每項活動。許多居民認為改善無障礙設施的錢花得值得。
listening.promptZh: money well spent 在這裏表示甚麼？

options.en: The cost produced a worthwhile accessibility benefit.
options.zh: 這筆開支帶來值得的無障礙改善。

options.en: The ramps must have been free.
options.zh: 斜道一定免費。

options.en: Every resident agreed on every budget item.
options.zh: 每名居民都同意每項預算。

options.en: The festival spent all available cash without a result.
options.zh: 節慶花光可用現金卻沒有成果。

listening.explanationZh: 居民所肯定的是輪椅使用者能參與活動的具體好處。

reply.promptEn: Why did the library renew the large-print collection? Older readers had waited months for readable books, and the new copies are now borrowed every week.
reply.promptZh: （圖書館為何更新大字版藏書？年長讀者等了幾個月才有容易閱讀的書，新書現時每週都有借出。）

options.en: The purchase answered a documented need.
options.zh: 採購回應了已知需要。

options.en: Readers are using the new books regularly.
options.zh: 讀者正定期借閱新書。

options.en: The library considers the purchase money well spent.
options.zh: 圖書館認為這筆採購花得值得。

options.en: The new copies improved access for waiting readers.
options.zh: 新書改善了等候讀者的閱讀機會。

reply.explanationZh: 四句均以有需要且實際使用解釋值得；金句用 money well spent。

scene.promptZh: 學校買了可重複使用的水壺，學生每日使用，亦減少即棄杯。哪句最貼切？

options.en: The bottles may be money well spent because they are used and reduce waste.
options.zh: 水壺每日有用，亦減少廢物，這筆錢可能花得值得。

options.en: They are worthwhile only if they cost nothing.
options.zh: 水壺只有免費才值得。

options.en: Any purchase is worthwhile once payment is complete.
options.zh: 只要付了錢，任何採購都值得。

scene.explanationZh: 有使用和減廢的具體成果。

contrast.promptZh: 哪項資料最能支持「花得值得」？

options.en: A learning kit cost more than expected but helped all six classes practise weekly.
options.zh: 學習工具價錢較預期高，卻讓六班每週都能練習。

options.en: A kit was bought and kept unopened in a cupboard.
options.zh: 工具買回後一直未開封，放在櫃裏。

options.en: The receipt confirms only that the school paid for a kit.
options.zh: 收據只證明學校付錢買了工具。

contrast.explanationZh: 判斷值得須有實際而相關的好處。

dialogue.promptZh: 朋友說：「這項目便宜，所以必然是 money well spent。」你怎樣回應？

options.en: A low price alone does not make it money well spent; ask what useful result the spending produced.
options.zh: 價錢低本身不足夠；要看開支帶來甚麼有用成果。

options.en: Anything cheap is automatically worthwhile.
options.zh: 任何便宜東西都自動值得。

options.en: The phrase means that all the money was spent.
options.zh: 這片語只表示錢已花光。

dialogue.explanationZh: 價值要看成果，不能只看標價。

speaking.en: Repairing the school lift was money well spent because pupils who use wheelchairs could finally reach the science rooms.
speaking.zh: 維修學校升降機的錢花得值得，因為使用輪椅的學生終於可到達科學室。
speaking.promptZh: 先聽示範，再指出改善帶來甚麼好處。

writing.promptZh: 新情境：社區中心花費兩萬元改善門口斜道，之前無法進入的輪椅使用者如今能參加每週課程；費用並不便宜，但中心認為有價值。用一至兩句英文解釋為何花得值得。
writing.selfCheckZh: 寫出兩萬元開支、斜道改善、輪椅使用者能參加每週課程；勿說因為便宜才值得。

examples.en: The centre called the twenty-thousand-dollar ramp money well spent because wheelchair users can now attend its weekly classes.
examples.zh: 中心認為花兩萬元改善斜道值得，因為輪椅使用者如今能參加每週課程。

examples.en: Although the twenty-thousand-dollar entrance ramp was not cheap, it was money well spent: people previously unable to enter can now join weekly activities.
examples.zh: 雖然兩萬元的門口斜道並不便宜，但這筆錢花得值得：之前無法進入的人如今可參加每週活動。

takeaways.en: Money well spent needs a worthwhile result, not just a low price.
takeaways.zh: 花得值得須有有價值的成果，不只是價格低。

takeaways.en: Call spending money well spent only when it brings a useful result.
takeaways.zh: 判斷一筆錢是否花得值時，要說明誰受益及如何受益。
